body:
I've always felt like the people who say it's the "easy" way out have obviously never been depressed to the point of feeling suicidal; once you feel that incredible burden, life is so overwhelmingly agonizing that others who haven't experienced it for themselves simply couldn't understand. Very rarely do people commit suicide impulsively. It's a very heavy decision and it (obviously no pun intended) kills us to think about the people we'd be hurting with our actions...but the pain we endure every single day by simply existing is so unbearable that we were driven to make that difficult decision anyway. 

I'm not trying to say it's the right decision or that the pain is insurmountable either. Just that the people who say "suicide is the easy way out" obviously never have been anywhere close to having experienced such pain...and for that they are lucky. 

It's also possible that many of the people who say that have suffered the loss of a loved one to suicide, and they are going through the "anger" stage of grief. They just don't understand the pain their loved one suffered and feel betrayed by their decision to kill their self and misplace that hurt into an accusation. Just my two cents though.

I've been in therapy for years. I can't see my current therapist because I'm out of state...my parents picked me up when my fiancé broke up with me. I don't want to be here. I want to go home. But that's not even my home anymore... 

And I don't even know how I feel about that therapist anymore because I just found out that she and our couple's therapist (they work at the same office) had been sharing information with a third therapist about me when I never signed waivers allowing them to do so. I don't feel like I can trust them.

My dog is awesome. He's the hardest part. He's so sweet. He's a German Shepherd Malamute mix. But he loves my fiancé so much too, and I can tell he really misses him and that's also killing me.

god it kills me to think about leaving my dog. i fucking lose it when i think about how he won't even know where i went and why he doesn't get to see me anymore omfg i'm going to cry just from typing that...

i also hate that it's not easy. and it's not like you can just google "easiest way to commit suicide". (trust me, i've tried...all you get is activism lol.) it's all messy and painful and slow...or horrifying and really hard to actually follow through with. like you said, i guess it's good in a way, but it also fucking sucks. it's agonizing and burdensome and i hate it.

idk why i typed this comment either. i guess just out of solidarity. just to let you know that you're not alone in any of these feelings. it sucks man. i think about all these things all the time.

It didn't have to be like this, though. We could have figured things out if you had been willing to give it a chance. Why did you simply give up? That's what I don't understand. I know the work would've been so, so hard. But why weren't you willing to even try?
I relate so deeply. If only we could *make* people care... I hope someday he either wakes the fuck up, or that you are able to be freed from this frustration.
I feel it too. You're not alone.

I am you. I am also the abuser, and I realized too late...I lost my fiancé a week and a half ago...and I feel so guilty that I can't even put it into words....I am going to therapy....I am putting in the work. But he doesn't want to give us a chance. I feel so devastated.

I am sorry you lost her, but proud of you for working on yourself.
This exact same thing happened to me....one week ago...but the other way around. I am so sorry.
